decidedBy: the project owner's direction of 2026-09-29 that the encyclopedia is this project's own and BibleData is kept for events and the timeline, applied to the records the dataset heads with a word that is nobody's and no place's name, and his ruling of 2026-09-30 on heaven, earth and the garden — recorded on TSK-0428
policy: A record is a person, a place or a people the text names, or something this project has read for itself. A dataset's record headed by a common noun or a description, with no word, verse, line, tie or picture of ours on it, is withdrawn. What the dataset says of it stays in the dataset's own files. The owner ruled heaven, earth and the garden out on 2026-09-30 although this corpus held a line, a name or a tie of its own on each: they are common words with several senses, not places. Those records are withdrawn with everything of ours that stood on them, and what the text says of Eden and of the trees that stood in it is held under Eden.

records.why: The waters of Genesis 1 are a common noun, mayim, and the seas they are gathered into; the text names no place by it.
Genesis 1:10 calls the gathered waters seas, a common noun; the dataset itself lists no verse for the record.
Daniel 11:21 says a vile person shall stand up, and gives him no name; the heading is the dataset's paraphrase of the description, and whom it means is a reading the text does not state.

Hebrew shamayim, heaven, is a common word with several senses: the firmament God called Heaven (GEN 1:8), where the lights are set (GEN 1:14-17) and the fowl fly (GEN 1:20). The text names no place by it.
